title:
RATIO,
(BEST VALUE PROBLEMS)
objective: LO: I can compare unit prices to determine which product offers the best value.

content.text: Best value means finding which option gives you the most for your money. Compare by finding the price per unit (or amount per penny).
Method: Divide price by quantity to find cost per unit. The lowest unit price is the best value.

examples.expr: The cheapest item is always best value

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Calculate the cost per unit for each option. The one with the lowest unit cost is the best value.
key_idea.caption: Compare unit prices: lowest = best value

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – two sizes
modelled_examples.question: Juice: 500ml for £1.20 or 1.5L for £3.00. Which is better value?
modelled_examples.explanation: Compare price per ml to find the best deal.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – three options
modelled_examples.question: Cereal: 400g for £2.80, 750g for £4.50, 1kg for £6.50. Best value?
modelled_examples.explanation: The biggest size is not always the best value.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – with special offer
modelled_examples.question: Milk: 2 pints for £1.10 or 4 pints for £1.80 (buy 2 get 10% off). Which?
steps: 4 pints with 10% off: £1.62, so 162 ÷ 4 = 40.5p per pint
4 pints with offer is better value
modelled_examples.explanation: Apply the discount before calculating unit price.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – amount per pound
modelled_examples.question: Shop A: 6 apples for £1.50. Shop B: 10 apples for £2.80. Best value?
steps: Shop A is cheaper per apple
modelled_examples.explanation: You can also compare apples per pound if preferred.

items.statement: Best value means lowest unit price
The biggest pack is always best value
To compare, divide price by quantity
The cheapest total price is always the best value

problems.text: A family needs 5 litres of milk per week. Options: 1 pint (568ml) for 55p, 2 pints for £1.00, 4 pints for £1.75, 6 pints for £2.40. What is the cheapest way to buy at least 5 litres?

Two phone contracts: Plan A: £25/month, 10GB data, unlimited calls. Plan B: £18/month, 5GB data, 500 minutes. Extra data costs £5/GB, extra minutes cost 3p/min. Which plan is better value if you use 8GB data and 400 minutes per month?
